chapter: Los Angeles: Roy Milton and Central Avenue
title: Hollywood clubs: Radio Room, Hangover and the Empire Room
summary: Lucky Thompson at the Radio Room, Dixieland at the Hangover, and Woody Herman's Four Brothers.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Well, we were like the session group. And when Dexter was on, Dexter was here. And Lucky Thompson, the fine tenor saxophone player, he had migrated to California with Boyd Raeburn's big band, and they played at the Radio Room up on Vine, between Selma and Hollywood Boulevard.
Yeah. And they had another place up from Billy Berg's called The Hangover, where the Dixieland players used to play...

Pete Daley, yeah. And that's where I first heard Ernie Caceres, the great baritone saxophone player. In fact, he seemed to be more advanced musically than the other guys that he was playing with. That's how he really impressed me when I heard him play, you know.

Right, right. Then they had the Empire Room on the west side of the street, just north of there. And that's where I first heard Woody Herman's band. That's when he had the Four Brothers and Ralph Burns and Dave Tough... He had a lot of really great players with the band during that period.

Right. Right, that was a great deal, and that's where I first heard the Four Brothers. But I had met Stan Getz before that, when he was living here in Hollywood, you know, and when I was playing at the Swing Club -- which I will go through a little later on.
